Wizard. Started with decent stats: 12 str, 16 dex. That's probably what got me as far as I got. Swapped my staff for a dagger to get the proficiency up early.

Took the fork to Minetown, which was uncharacteristically rough. Nothing crazy spawned; just more of it, and at times so inopportune as to seem calculated. Multiple visits from Team Ant. I ended up reaching Minetown being chased by a swarm of killer bees, and no energy. The situation in town wasn't immediately terrible, which is good because I couldn't go back up without using up magic marker charges scribbling Elbereth. I locked a guard inside a deli (they can't get in the way of they're trapped in a closet) and Izchak sold me a magic lamp. Fortuitous.

Obviously, I want to BUC test that lamp and wish for SDSM. Silver makes particular sense in Minetown as the reflection would allow me to murder the priest with relative impunity from Thoth's thunderous attempts to punish my impiety. Being Chaotic, I'd possibly sack the priest to convert the altar, and do what it takes to get Magicbane.

No such luck. On the way to the temple I got ambushed over and over again. I had plenty of food, but having to retreat to a closet I found that I didn't have quite enough life and energy to fight my way back out. I had to wait to recover, and the monsters spawned too fast to break the siege. I'd unlock the door, unload into a pack of wolves, only to then have to stab a pack of uruk-hai to death, only to then be attacked by a mumak, a swarm of bees, and various other assholes who run faster than I do.

I had resisted, but there was no other choice but to dig downward.

A white unicorn dogged me across the next floor, until it stepped on a sleeping trap. Knowing better than to trust in force bolt, I spent some magic missile charges to dispatch it. Sure enough, even with that I had to fire eight times. But then I had a unicorn horn, and could now recover the strength lost from eating bugs— I never did get poison immunity— and from random, periodic attrition of my ability scores because "I haven't been paying attention!"

The bottom floor had the usual undead party zone, featuring a vampire lord right in my face. I brought him upstairs and zapped him with a teleport wand. Never saw him again, curiously. But of course, by this point my inventory was full and I hadn't encountered a single bag, so there was no sense exploring further.

It was a smooth enough walk back to Minetown. I climbed the stairs at full power. The siege army from before immediately began filing in. An unidentified wand turned a mumak and a leopard into a grid bug and a newt. A warhorse attacking at the same time refused a tripe ration— they're apparently vegetarian, but a peaceful animal is about as useful as friendly one.

Finally had the breathing room to rub one out, so I tested and tried the lamp. Angry genie. Figures.

As a rule, I'm reluctant to hang on to stuff I'd otherwise horde, if I had a bag of holding. Without a bag, I spent my three scrolls of identify identifying, in turn, 2 potions of booze, a potion of monster detection, and a potion of object detection. Real goddamn life savers, but at least I could dilute them into a single stack of water, and if I lived long enough, pray them into holy water.

Naturally, this still wasn't the end of the dickery, and I found it necessary to zap myself with a wand of invisibility to make my way back out of the mines. That left me wishing I'd taken a mummy wrapping; I had no way to get into a general store further down into the dungeon.

It took almost no time to bump into a soldier ant in a dark corridor and die instantly. I have feelings about this outcome.

I'm thinking the best thing to do is to hit minetown to see if the altar is cross-aligned. If not, I might as well do sokoban first.
